WEB-03a781657bb4.title: Funding Opportunities
WEB-03a781657bb4.summary: This page outlines multiple distinct funding opportunities from the Brain Canada Foundation rather than a single research funding call. Listed initiatives include the 2026 Future Leaders in Canadian Brain Research, the CanNRT-Brain Canada Fellowship, the 2026 Knowledge Mobilization Grants, and Innovation & Impact Grants. Each opportunity has separate objectives, funding levels, eligibility requirements, and deadlines for researchers, trainees, and clinician scientists studying brain health.
WEB-03a781657bb4.eligible_countries: Not stated in the official text: check the call

WEB-00773cbd93aa.title: Bridge Funding for Disrupted Neurodegenerative Research Grant Program (BFDN) Powering the Next Generation of Research
WEB-00773cbd93aa.programme: Bridge Funding for Disrupted Neurodegenerative Research (BFDN) grant program
WEB-00773cbd93aa.summary: This program supports early-career investigators whose research projects on Alzheimer's, Parkinson's, and related neurodegenerative disorders were disrupted by operational or priority changes in U.S. federal funding. Grants provide up to $250,000 for 3 to 12 months to cover salary and direct research costs, requiring up to 25% institutional cost-sharing. Eligible principal investigators must meet NIH Early Stage Investigator definitions (or be within seven years of designation) and have experienced specific disruptions to federal grants.
WEB-00773cbd93aa.eligible_countries: Not stated in the official text: check the call

GG-HT942526PRPEIRA.title: DoW Parkinson's, Early Investigator Research Award
GG-HT942526PRPEIRA.summary: The FY26 Parkinson’s Research Program Early Investigator Research Award supports Parkinson’s disease research by investigators in the early stages of their careers. Proposed research must address at least one of four program focus areas; clinical trials are not allowed. Two funding levels are offered: Funding Level 1 for fellows (requiring guidance from an experienced mentor) and Funding Level 2 for early-career independent investigators (requiring preliminary data). Applicant eligibility is unrestricted.
GG-HT942526PRPEIRA.eligible_countries: Not stated in the official text: check the call

GG-HT942526PRPIIRA.title: DoW Parkinson's, Investigator-Initiated Research Award
GG-HT942526PRPIIRA.summary: The FY26 Parkinson’s Research Program Investigator-Initiated Research Award supports rigorous, multidisciplinary research projects with the potential to make significant contributions to Parkinson’s disease research. Projects must address at least one FY26 PRP focus area, with clinical trials allowed and preliminary data required. Eligibility is unrestricted by entity type, and applications may include a Partnering Principal Investigator option with one initiating PI and up to two partnering PIs.
GG-HT942526PRPIIRA.eligible_countries: Not stated in the official text: check the call

GG-HT942526SCIRPTRA.title: DoW Spinal Cord Injury, Translational Research Award
GG-HT942526SCIRPTRA.summary: The FY26 Spinal Cord Injury Research Program Translational Research Award supports translational research aimed at moving promising ideas into clinical applications for spinal cord injury. Funding supports translational projects, including an Early-Career Partnership Option with two principal investigators. Applications must include at least one community partner with lived experience. Eligible applicant types are unrestricted, open to any type of entity subject to clarification in the full announcement.
GG-HT942526SCIRPTRA.eligible_countries: Not stated in the official text: check the call

GG-HT942526SCIRPCTA.title: DoW Spinal Cord Injury, Clinical Trial Award
GG-HT942526SCIRPCTA.summary: The Spinal Cord Injury Research Program Clinical Trial Award supports the rapid implementation of clinical trials with the potential to significantly impact the treatment or management of spinal cord injury. Funding supports clinical trials, featuring an Early-Career Partnership Option that allows two Principal Investigators. Applications are open to unrestricted applicant types, but must include at least two spinal cord injury community partners who provide consultation and advice throughout the project.
GG-HT942526SCIRPCTA.eligible_countries: Not stated in the official text: check the call

GG-HT942526SCIRPCTRA.title: DoW Spinal Cord Injury, Clinical Translation Research Award
GG-HT942526SCIRPCTRA.summary: The FY26 Spinal Cord Injury Research Program Clinical Translation Research Award supports high-impact, new, or emerging clinical research requiring preliminary studies—such as feasibility, pilot, or optimization—to prepare for future larger-scale clinical trials or implementation. It aims to accelerate translation of interventions into clinical use and improve diagnosis, treatment, and rehabilitation options. Applicant types are unrestricted, with mandatory inclusion of at least two spinal cord injury community partners.
GG-HT942526SCIRPCTRA.eligible_countries: Not stated in the official text: check the call

GG-HT942526SCIRPIIRA.title: DoW Spinal Cord Injury, Investigator-Initiated Research Award
GG-HT942526SCIRPIIRA.summary: The FY26 Spinal Cord Injury Research Program Investigator-Initiated Research Award supports studies that make significant contributions to spinal cord injury research, patient care, or quality of life. Funding covers projects across basic through translational science, while studies solely identifying intervention targets are discouraged. Eligible applicant types are unrestricted. Additionally, an Early-Career Partnership Option allows two Principal Investigators to submit applications, provided at least one is an early-career investigator.
GG-HT942526SCIRPIIRA.eligible_countries: Not stated in the official text: check the call

GG-PAR-25-226.title: Seamless Early-Stage Clinical Drug Development (Phase 1 to 2a) for Novel therapeutic Agents for AD/ADRD
GG-PAR-25-226.programme_family: NIH – US National Institutes of Health
GG-PAR-25-226.summary: This funding opportunity supports the early-stage clinical drug development of novel, non-amyloid and non-tau therapeutic candidates for Alzheimer's disease and related dementias. It funds phased projects that bundle phase 1 clinical trials (UG3) with phase 1b/2a trials (UH3) to evaluate safety, dosing, pharmacokinetics, and target engagement. Applications are open to higher education institutions, nonprofits, for-profit businesses, and foreign non-U.S. organizations.
GG-PAR-25-226.countries_evidence: Non-domestic (non-U.S.) Entities (Foreign Organizations) are eligible to apply.
